description: Direction Sense is a crucial topic under Logical Reasoning. It involves determining the specific direction and distance of a person or object from their initial starting position to their final position.

sections.title: Main and Sub-Directions
sections.description: Basic knowledge of directions is the fundamental requirement for solving Direction Sense questions accurately.

key_concepts.explanation: There are four primary directions: North, South, East, and West.
There are four sub-directions located exactly midway between the main directions: North-East, North-West, South-East, and South-West.
The angle between two adjacent main directions is 90°, while the angle between a main direction and its adjacent sub-direction is exactly 45°.

sections.title: Turns and Rotations
sections.description: Questions frequently require a person to navigate by turning left or right from their current facing direction.

key_concepts.explanation: Moving in the direction of the clock hands, which equates to turning to the right side.
Moving in the opposite direction of the clock hands, which equates to turning to the left side.

results: Unless a specific angle is mentioned, every turn must be assumed as a 90° turn by default.
If a person is facing North, taking a right turn will make them face East.
Taking two consecutive right turns or two consecutive left turns (180° total) brings a person to face the exact opposite of their initial direction.

sections.title: Shortest Distance
sections.description: Calculating the minimum straight-line distance between the starting point and the ending point of a journey.

key_concepts.explanation: The longest side of a right-angled triangle formed by the path, representing the shortest aerial distance.
The total vertical and horizontal distances covered during the respective movements.

sections.title: Shadow-based Concept
sections.description: Determining the facing direction of a person based on the shadows formed during sunrise and sunset.

results: The sun rises in the East.
The shadow of any object or person will always fall towards the West.
If a person's shadow falls exactly in front of them, it means they are facing West.
The sun sets in the West.
The shadow of any object or person will always fall towards the East.
The rays of the sun are vertically downward (directly overhead).
No shadow is formed at this exact time.

sections.title: Steps to Solve Problems
sections.description: A systematic graphical approach to accurately trace the path and solve Direction Sense questions.

steps.title: Determine Starting Point
steps.detail: Assume the center of your rough page as the starting point and draw a small cross (+) as a reference axis.

steps.title: Draw a Proportional Diagram
steps.detail: Draw lines mapping the journey according to the question. Keep distances visibly proportional (e.g., a 10 km line must be drawn visibly longer than a 5 km line).

steps.title: Map the Directions
steps.detail: Always assume the top of your page as North, the bottom as South, the right side as East, and the left side as West while drawing.

steps.title: Final Calculation
steps.detail: Connect the start and end points. Use the Pythagoras theorem for diagonal endpoints or simple addition/subtraction for straight-line endpoints to find the final distance and direction.
